items.title: Trat
items.description: In the riverside town of Trat, cozy noodle joints, seafood restaurants, and specialty stores line bustling Sukhumvit Road and the surrounding residential streets. It's home to the striking Trat City Museum, which highlights local history and culture. Colorful flower beds and tree-lined paths draw locals and visitors to Trat Provincial Botanical Garden, while Si Sat Reservoir attracts birders and sunset photographers. ― Google

![Trat travel guide - Activities, Events & Things to do](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07270106-1672-0139-0000-e3e816d8d519:5)
Trat is `an eastern Thai province known as the main gateway to tropical islands like Koh Chang, Koh Kood, and Koh Mak` . It sits about 300 kilometers from Bangkok, bordering Cambodia, and offers rich seafood, quiet fishing villages, and coral reefs.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trat_province) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trat_province)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/trtworld/videos/thailand-holiday-hotspots-affected-by-border-clashes/861414849855875/)[[3]](https://fanclubthailand.co.uk/trat/)[[4]](https://www.agoda.com/en-gb/city/trat-th.html)[[5]](https://iamkohchang.com/guide/trat-town.html)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CBcP0h-W2BM&t=1)[[7]](https://www.tourismthailand.org/Destinations/Provinces/Trat/466)

Top Islands

- **Koh Chang:** Thailand's third-largest island, featuring big hills, waterfalls, and long beaches.
- **Koh Kood:** A quiet, slow-paced island with clear water and green nature.
- **Koh Mak:** A flat, peaceful island filled with coconut trees and quiet sand spots.[](https://fanclubthailand.co.uk/trat/) [[1]](https://www.facebook.com/SeatranFerry/posts/announcementto-cooperate-with-the-government-measures-due-to-the-current-situati/3551088744982471/)[[2]](https://www.wideeyedtours.com/thailand/koh-chang)[[3]](https://www.aanaresort.com/blog-details.php?&id=1)[[4]](https://travelhappy.info/one-week-thailands-beaches-guide/)

Things to Do in Trat Town

- **Night Market:** Try cheap, fresh local seafood and sweet Thai snacks.
- **Ban Nam Chiao:** Visit this local village to see mixed Thai-Buddhist and Muslim cultures and unique local crafts.
- **Trat Museum:** Learn old local history and stories about the sea trade.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CBcP0h-W2BM&t=1) 

Travel Tips

- **Best Time to Go:** November to February brings cooler and drier days. May to October brings heavy rain.
- **How to Get There:** You can ride a 6-hour bus from Bangkok or take a short flight to Trat's small airport. Ferries connect the mainland to the islands.[](https://www.agoda.com/en-gb/city/trat-th.html) [[1]](https://www.theblondtravels.com/trat-thailand-experience)

items.title: Is Trat, Thailand worth visiting?

expanded_element.title: The Ultimate Trat Travel Guide - Thailand Starts Here
expanded_element.description: Is Trat worth visiting? Trat isn't an especially easy place to visit, but it can be worth it if you set realistic expectations and use your time well. More to the point, I wouldn't recommend Trat as a weekend trip from Bangkok, but think spending a week island hopping is a very good use of your time.

items.title: Is it safe to go to Trat, Thailand right now?

expanded_element.title: Thailand Travel Advice & Safety | Smartraveller
expanded_element.description: We advise do not travel to areas within 10 kilometres of the Thailand-Cambodia land border in the provinces of Sa Kaeo, Buriram, Si Saket, Surin, Ubon Ratchathani, Chanthaburi and mainland Trat. All border crossing points along the Thailand-Cambodia border are currently closed.

items.title: How do I get to Trat, Thailand?

expanded_element.title: Trat: It's all about the experience | The Blond Travels
expanded_element.description: Trat has a very small airport and you can take a flight to and from Bangkok. There are also buses from Morchit Bangkok directly to Trat. The journey takes 6 hours and tickets cost around 350 Baht. If you're traveling from Chanthaburi, you will be able to catch a direct bus to Trat from the main bus station.

expanded_element.description: The distance between Bangkok and Trat province (State) is 312 km. The road distance is 310.9 km. How do I travel from Bangkok to Trat province (State) without a car? The best way to get from Bangkok to Trat province (State) without a car is to bus which takes 5h 30m and costs ฿280 - ฿2500.
